drivingQuestion: Does the baraita limit the larger ketuba to marriages with a priestly aspect?

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים עוֹשִׂין, כְּגוֹן בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן, וּבַת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל — עוֹשִׂין. בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן וּבַת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דְּאִיכָּא צַד כְּהוּנָּה. אֲבָל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל — לָא!
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection» from a baraita: «One who sought to act as the priests do,» as in cases «where an Israelite woman» is married «to a priest, or the daughter of a priest» is married «to an Israelite, may act» in that manner. The Gemara infers: This allowance is specifically in cases where «an Israelite woman» is married «to a priest, or the daughter of a priest» is married «to an Israelite, where there is an aspect of priesthood» involved. «However,» apparently, in a case where «the daughter of an Israelite» is married «to an Israelite, no,» it is not allowed.

segments.he: לָא מִבַּעְיָא קָאָמַר: לָא מִבַּעְיָא בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּלָא מָצֵי אָמַר לַהּ עַלּוֹיֵי קָא מְעַלֵּינָא לִיךְ, אֲבָל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן, דְּמָצֵי אָמַר לַהּ עַלּוֹיֵי קָא מְעַלֵּינָא לִיךְ — אֵימָא לָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects that inference. The baraita «is stated» employing the style of: «It is not necessary. It is not necessary» to state a case where «the daughter of an Israelite» is married «to an Israelite, as» in that case the groom «cannot say to her:» By marrying you, «I am raising your» social status, and it is clear that women from distinguished families would demand a marriage contract with a greater sum. «However,» in a case where «an Israelite woman» is married «to a priest, where he can say to her: I am raising your» social status, as you are marrying into the priesthood, you might think to «say no,» the woman cannot demand a marriage contract with a greater sum. Therefore, the baraita «teaches us» that even in the case of a woman from a distinguished family of Israelites marrying a priest, she may demand a marriage contract with a greater sum.
